question: Should v1 standardize the proposed canonical condition schema together with activation-scoped plugin readiness providers and explicit `gateway.readiness` criteria selection?
rationale: The patch is technically coherent, but it commits OpenClaw to new core configuration and plugin API surfaces whose permanent ownership and compatibility policy cannot be selected by automated review.

options.title: Accept the scoped v1
options.body: Adopt canonical conditions, opt-in criteria, and activation-scoped providers while preserving every legacy projection and default behavior.

options.title: Land core conditions first
options.body: Accept the canonical evaluator and compatibility projections now, but defer plugin providers and operator-selected criteria to a follow-up RFC.

options.title: Keep the fixed evaluator
options.body: Decline the new public contract and continue evolving readiness through core-owned observations only.

recommendation.title: Accept the scoped v1
recommendation.body: Adopt canonical conditions, opt-in criteria, and activation-scoped providers while preserving every legacy projection and default behavior.

likelyOwner.reason: Recent history shows the strongest ownership signal for Gateway startup and lifecycle behavior, which is the central product boundary under decision.
